name: Pancharama Kshetras
theme: Five ancient Shiva temples of the Krishna and Godavari deltas, marking where the shattered lingam of the demon Taraka came to rest
description: When Kumara Swamy slew the demon Tarakasura, the great Shiva lingam the demon had worn could not be destroyed; broken apart, its five pieces flew across the Telugu country and set themselves in the earth, and the gods fixed and consecrated each where it fell. These are the Pancharama Kshetras — five ancient Shiva temples strung across the Krishna and Godavari deltas of coastal Andhra: Amararama at Amaravati above the Krishna, Somarama at Bhimavaram whose lingam changes hue with the moon, Ksheerarama at Palakollu with its soaring white gopuram, the great two-storeyed Draksharama that is also a Shakti Peetha, and Kumararama at Samalkota. Many were raised by the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi, and together they make one of the most cherished pilgrimages of the Andhra country.
